title: Saints Martha, Mary, and Lazarus
short_summary: Saints Martha, Mary, and Lazarus are honored as friends of the Lord at Bethany, witnesses of hospitality, listening, and faith in Christ the Resurrection and the Life.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps their memorial on July 29.
The memorial was designated for Saints Martha, Mary, and Lazarus in the General Roman Calendar in 2021.
John's Gospel says Jesus loved Martha, Mary, and Lazarus.
The profile should not conflate Mary of Bethany with other women beyond what the Church's source supports.

sections.heading: Friends of the Lord
sections.body: The Bethany household gives the Church a Gospel picture of friendship with Jesus. Martha welcomes him, Mary listens, and Lazarus becomes a sign of Christ's power over death.

sections.heading: Martha's confession
sections.body: In John 11, Martha confesses faith in Jesus as the Christ and hears him reveal himself as the Resurrection and the Life. Her witness is doctrinally rich and deeply personal.

sections.heading: A careful calendar change
sections.body: The Holy See expanded the July 29 memorial from Saint Martha alone to Saints Martha, Mary, and Lazarus. The change is rooted in their evangelical witness as a household loved by Christ.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Welcoming Christ
catholic_connection_sections.body: Their memorial honors hospitality, listening, and faith as responses to the Lord who came among them in the Gospel.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Resurrection faith
catholic_connection_sections.body: Lazarus's raising and Martha's confession point beyond Bethany to Christ's victory over death.

historical_cautions: Do not merge Mary of Bethany with Mary Magdalene or other Gospel women beyond what the Church's cited decree explains.
